subject: Is manually setting factor contrasts in colext model possible?

messages.author: e6ea535446304d42
messages.subject: Is manually setting factor contrasts in colext model possible?
parts:
I am analysing a multi-season occupancy data set that has a treatment applied to ~50% of sites each year. It is the same treatment each year to the same sets of sites, but I am interested in finding whether the treatment has the same or different effect each season.

I have coded the YearlySiteCovs of Treatment with a combination of treatment and year, e.g. “Y17”, “N17”, “Y18”, “N18”,”Y19”,”N19” for yes/no treatment in 2017, 2018 and 2019. When analysing using colext with Treatment as a factor in gamma and/or epsilon formulas it successfully runs, but the summary output compares each level of the Treatment factor to the base/intercept value, which by default is the first listed alphabetically “N17”. This default can be changed by setting levels() of the factor and reordering so the required base level is first, but still does not allow me to specify pairwise comparisons within years, such as “N18” vs “Y18”.

When using LM/GLM/GLMM etc you can set the contrasts for levels of a factor manually, and it is also possible to set these in the unmarkedMultFrame for the factor. E.g.:

contrasts(umf@yearlySiteCovs$Treatment) <- my.contrasts

but this does not appear to affect the model in any way.

1)      Is there a way to manually specify contrasts for factors in a colext (or occu) model, or have I asked too much of the package?

2)      Given I can manually set the levels() of the factor, I could conceivably change the base level and re-run the model several times to receive the individual a priori pairwise contrasts I am interested in. Would this be a useable workaround or am I breaking other assumptions with this approach?

 

Many thanks,

Alistair
